system_description.narrative_title: A System in Flux: Tech Turmoil, Great‑Power Friction and Climate Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The international order is an open, tightly coupled system being reshaped by a convergence of shocks: a politically volatile United States whose midterm outcome is rewiring policy and markets; a destabilising new phase of great‑power and regional conflict (notably Russia‑Ukraine and Iran‑Gulf dynamics) with active military strikes and quiet mediation; and an accelerating techno‑economic reconfiguration as AI and data‑centre expansion collide with market corrections, public pushback and fiscal pressures. These dynamics interact with an intensifying climate impulse — rising physical risks and policy responses — and with uneven economic performance (inflation, central‑bank tightening, weak demand in major economies), producing rapid feedbacks, cross‑domain spillovers and high systemic uncertainty.
system_description.scope: Nation‑states, their military and diplomatic interactions, transnational institutions (NATO, EU, IMF, UN), global markets and finance, multinational tech and energy infrastructures (AI/data centres, energy supply chains), climate policy processes (COP), and major regional conflict theatres (Ukraine, Middle East).
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio‑political‑economic system (interdependent global economy, security architecture, and Earth system/climate)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and capital flows

variables.name: Middle East maritime escalation
variables.description: Iran, its regional proxies (notably the Houthis), Saudi Arabia and the U.S. are engaged in an intensifying campaign of missile and maritime attacks that is raising the risk of wider regional conflict and disrupting shipping security.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and European security
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a prolonged war marked by cross-border strikes, attacks on critical infrastructure and contested planning among European states over the depth and form of military responses, shifting the continent's security architecture.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic competition
variables.description: The United States and China are escalating a broad strategic rivalry across trade, state-level tech controls, space and communications capabilities and diplomatic influence, reshaping global strategic alignments and supply-chain policy.

variables.name: AI and data‑infrastructure backlash
variables.description: Governments, investors and societies are reacting to rapid AI buildouts and their infrastructure — triggering protests at data‑center sites, financing stress, IPO setbacks and accelerating regulatory and corporate governance responses that are reordering the tech industry.

variables.name: U.S. political realignment and policy shift
variables.description: A major domestic political realignment in the United States — driven by election outcomes and intra‑party change — is altering personnel, congressional oversight and the policymaking trajectory that will determine U.S. responses abroad and the implementation of sanctions, probes and diplomacy.
